outcomes.text: Explain how personal viewpoint, experience and context shape responses to texts.
Explain how mode, medium and form shape responses.
Tell initial personal responses from more studied, complex ones.
Recognise that reader and viewer responses range from empathetic to critical.
Analyse how structure, language and style create meaning and nuance, for example through allusion, paradox and ambiguity.
Identify different points of view, such as characters, narrators and implied author.
Analyse approaches to characterisation, including archetypes, authorial intrusion and interior monologue.
Analyse narrative approaches such as multiple, unreliable and omniscient narrators.
Analyse figurative language and rhetoric such as symbolism, metonymy, irony and imagery patterns.
Analyse sound and visual devices like assonance, prosody, rhyme, animation and voice-over.
Structure arguments and viewpoints with relevant textual evidence.
Use linguistic, stylistic and critical terminology when responding.
Use stylistic features to craft and express viewpoints.
Experiment with different modes, mediums and forms.
Connect real and imagined experiences.
Draw on knowledge of storytelling, style and text structure.
Experiment with style and form for deliberate effect.
Reflect on familiar and emerging literary forms for particular audiences.
Explain how texts are influenced by other texts and by contexts.
Relate genre conventions and audience expectations to interpretation.
Explain how choosing and combining mode, medium and form transforms texts.
Explain how informed reading influences interpretation.
Explain how structure, features and style frame audience expectations and interpretation.
Analyse parody, imitation, appropriation and adaptation and the insights they give into originals.
Examine how literary elements enter popular culture through iconic situations, symbols or characters.
Examine how literary forms evolve, such as digital storytelling.
Evaluate poetic, dramatic and narrative structures and devices.
Evaluate combined sound and visual devices such as soundtracks, cinematography and iconography.
Organise viewpoints and arguments in forms like essays, reviews and visual presentations.
Use critical terminology to compare and contrast texts.
Select suitable argument and evidence to support viewpoints.
Experiment with different modes, mediums and forms.
Blend real and imagined experience by adapting aspects of texts into new ones.
Use literary analysis to inform imaginative response.
Transform a text from one medium or genre to another for new audiences.
Reflect on the significance and effects of variations to texts.

topics.title: Culture and identity in literary texts

outcomes.text: Evaluate how readers are influenced to respond to their own and others' cultural experiences.
Evaluate the power of language to represent ideas, events and people in particular ways.
Evaluate how cultural perceptions are challenged or supported.
Evaluate how authors represent Australian culture, place and identity.
Relate significant historical and cultural events and figures to their literary representations.
Evaluate the impact of literary conventions and stylistic techniques.
Judge the effectiveness of conventions such as iambic pentameter, stream of consciousness, flashback and chorus.
Explain how language and style communicate values and attitudes and give fresh light on familiar ideas.
Develop independent interpretations backed by informed observation and close analysis.
Use critical terminology to analyse and evaluate texts.
Evaluate own and others' ideas using logic and evidence.
Experiment with different modes, mediums and forms.
Experiment with content, form, style, language and medium.
Use genre, literary devices and visual-verbal interplay to create new texts.
Adapt and challenge conventions and reinterpret ideas for specific audiences.
Reflect on how form, style, language and content engage and position the audience.

subtopics.title: Change, audience and interpretation over time

outcomes.text: Evaluate how literature reflects cultural change and difference.
Evaluate how audience expectations and values shape perceptions of texts.
Compare texts from different forms, mediums or traditions.
Explain how interpretations of texts vary over time.
Evaluate how perspectives from other times and cultures are conveyed and renewed for a contemporary Australian audience.
Evaluate how ideas, values and assumptions are conveyed.
Evaluate how elements like mise-en-scene, enjambment, dramatic monologue and verse drama shape meaning.
Explain how medium, form, language and wordplay contribute to interpretation.
Explore a range of critical interpretations.
Develop a creative, informed, sustained interpretation backed by close analysis.
Use critical terminology to evaluate and justify interpretations.
Critically evaluate own and others' justifications, evidence and viewpoints.
Experiment with different modes, mediums and forms.
Adapt medium, form, style, viewpoint and language.
Experiment with style and voice for specific effects.
Manipulate literary conventions for different audiences and contexts.
Reflect on how audience expectations and values shape the created text.
